criteria.rationale: Additive and proven so: parsing the policy before and after shows two keys added, none removed and none changed, so the thirty-line diff is MarshalIndent reordering the document alphabetically. The installed 5.0.8 binary resolves a review plan against the reordered policy, exit 0. The stamp changes no bundle: whether one is governed is decided by the engine that sealed it, so no existing review gained or lost an obligation.

No code in this change set: two dated policy keys, a machinery manifest of hashes and three regenerated indexes. The checks that answer this criterion report on the pose-mcp module, which this change does not touch, so citing them would be a passing test run presented as proof of something else. What verified the change is the before-and-after key-set comparison of the policy itself, recorded in the trace.

The spec states what the stamp does and, as plainly, what it does not: it adds no enforcement. The reordering is documented as accepted rather than hidden, with the reason the engine rewrites the whole document. The self-referential behaviour the run reported - POSE.md skipped as an unresolved scaffold placeholder - is recorded too, because in this repository that skip is the protection and not a failure.

The run was idempotent and its scope was confirmed against a clean tree: only the policy and the machinery manifest changed, and the machinery merges were no-ops. Reverting is reverting one commit. Removing the dates would not remove the contracts from any sealed bundle, which is what makes this safe to reverse.
Same reason and same evidence classes as correctness: no code path under test. R1 to R4 are each traced to a measurement taken against this repository before and after the stamp.

Four claims reconciled against four Git-observed paths, then the three regenerated indexes declared once measured. The spec declares no component, which is what a policy-and-manifest change is, and that is why two mechanical criteria are not-applicable rather than answered with an unrelated module run. Activating the ABM overlay profiles was deliberately left out as a separate decision.

The stamp grants nothing and loosens nothing: overlay_profiles was verified unchanged, so no independence floor, identity assurance or attestation requirement moved, and the key-set comparison proves no other policy value changed. The grandfathering it enables is dated and bounded to scopes already completed, so it cannot excuse a review recorded after it. Three completed specs were confirmed still approved and terminal.

tools.rationale: No code in the change set to carry a TODO, FIXME, panic or stub.
No delivery target is declared, so the delivery-gated check has nothing to compose. Recorded as deferred rather than passed on an unrelated module run.
